subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Ionic bonding occurs between which types of element?
options: A metal and a non-metal
Two non-metals
Two metals
Two noble gases
questions.explain: Ionic bonds form when a metal transfers electrons to a non-metal, producing oppositely charged ions.

questions.q: When a sodium atom forms an ion, what happens to its electrons?
options: It loses one electron to form Na+
It gains one electron to form Na-
It gains two electrons to form Na2-
It loses two electrons to form Na2+
questions.explain: Sodium has one electron in its outer shell, which it loses to gain a stable full outer shell and a 1+ charge.

questions.q: Which term best describes the structure of solid sodium chloride?
options: A giant ionic lattice
A simple molecule
A giant covalent structure
A sea of delocalised electrons
questions.explain: Sodium chloride consists of a regular repeating three-dimensional lattice of oppositely charged ions held by strong electrostatic forces.

options: A shared pair of electrons between two atoms
A transfer of electrons from one atom to another
An attraction between positive ions and delocalised electrons
A force between neighbouring molecules
questions.explain: In a covalent bond, two atoms share a pair of electrons, giving each a share of a stable outer shell.

questions.q: Covalent bonding typically occurs between which types of atom?
options: Non-metal atoms
A metal and a non-metal
Metal atoms only
Positive ions
questions.explain: Covalent bonds form between non-metal atoms that share electrons rather than transferring them.

questions.q: How many covalent bonds are present in a molecule of methane, CH4?
questions.explain: Carbon forms four single covalent bonds, one to each of the four hydrogen atoms.

questions.q: Metallic bonding is best described as the attraction between which particles?
options: Positive metal ions and a sea of delocalised electrons
Positive and negative ions
Shared pairs of electrons between atoms
Neutral atoms and neutrons
questions.explain: In a metal, positive ions are held in a lattice by a shared 'sea' of delocalised outer-shell electrons.

options: They contain delocalised electrons that are free to move
They contain ions that vibrate faster when heated
They are made of simple molecules
They have weak forces between layers
questions.explain: The delocalised electrons in a metal can move through the structure and carry electrical charge.

questions.q: Why do ionic compounds generally have high melting points?
options: Strong electrostatic forces between ions need a lot of energy to overcome
Weak intermolecular forces are easily broken
Covalent bonds within molecules are broken on melting
Delocalised electrons hold the lattice together weakly
questions.explain: The many strong electrostatic attractions in a giant ionic lattice require a large amount of energy to break.

questions.q: Why does solid sodium chloride not conduct electricity, but molten sodium chloride does?
options: In the solid the ions are fixed in place, but when molten the ions are free to move
The solid has no charged particles, but melting creates new electrons
The molten form contains delocalised electrons only
Melting converts the ionic bonds into covalent bonds
questions.explain: Conduction requires charged particles that can move; ions are locked in the solid lattice but mobile once molten.

questions.q: Diamond and graphite are both giant covalent structures made from which element?
options: Carbon
Silicon
Sodium
Chlorine
questions.explain: Both diamond and graphite are forms (allotropes) of the element carbon.

options: Each carbon atom has a delocalised electron that is free to move
It contains free-moving positive ions
Its molecules are small and can move past each other
It has a full sea of shared electrons between all atoms
questions.explain: In graphite each carbon bonds to only three others, leaving one delocalised electron per atom that can carry charge.

options: Each carbon atom forms four strong covalent bonds in a rigid giant structure
It is held together by weak intermolecular forces
It contains layers that cannot slide
It has a sea of delocalised electrons
questions.explain: Every carbon in diamond is covalently bonded to four others, giving a rigid three-dimensional network.

questions.q: Magnesium oxide (MgO) has a much higher melting point than sodium chloride (NaCl). The best explanation is that:
options: MgO contains ions with higher charges, so the electrostatic forces are stronger
MgO is a simple molecular substance
NaCl contains delocalised electrons that weaken the lattice
MgO has covalent bonds and NaCl has ionic bonds
questions.explain: The 2+ and 2- ions in MgO attract more strongly than the 1+ and 1- ions in NaCl, requiring more energy to separate.

questions.q: Magnesium forms Mg2+ ions and chlorine forms Cl- ions. What is the formula of magnesium chloride?
options: MgCl2
MgCl
Mg2Cl
MgCl3
questions.explain: Two Cl- ions are needed to balance the 2+ charge of one Mg2+ ion, giving MgCl2.

questions.q: Simple molecular substances such as water usually have low melting and boiling points because:
options: The forces between molecules are weak and easily broken
The covalent bonds within molecules are weak
They contain a sea of delocalised electrons
They form giant lattices of ions
questions.explain: Only the weak intermolecular forces are overcome on melting or boiling, not the strong covalent bonds inside the molecules.

questions.q: A substance has a high melting point, does not conduct electricity when solid, but conducts when molten or dissolved in water. What type of bonding does it have?
options: Ionic
Simple molecular covalent
Metallic
Giant covalent
questions.explain: These are the characteristic properties of an ionic compound, whose ions become mobile only when molten or dissolved.

questions.q: Aluminium forms Al3+ ions and oxygen forms O2- ions. What is the formula of aluminium oxide?
options: Al2O3
AlO
Al3O2
AlO2
questions.explain: Balancing the charges requires two Al3+ (total 6+) and three O2- (total 6-), giving Al2O3.
